name: Seattle
operatingHours: Link light rail (1 and 2 Lines) runs ~5:00 AM–~1:00 AM Mon–Sat and ~6:00 AM–midnight Sun, every 8–15 min. Seattle Streetcar runs ~5:00 AM–~11:00 PM (shorter on Sundays); the Monorail runs ~7:30 AM–11:00 PM, every ~10 min. No all-night rail.
fareInfo: Link is a flat $3 adult fare for any trip (since Aug 2024), including the airport; tap an ORCA card (or the Transit GO app) on the platform reader before boarding and again to finish. Streetcar ~$3 and Monorail ~$4 per ride (2026). An ORCA card ($3) gives 2-hour transfers between Link, buses and streetcar; the Monorail takes ORCA and contactless cards but transfers don't apply.

sights.name: Chihuly Garden and Glass
sights.note: Dale Chihuly's blown-glass installations fill galleries, a glasshouse and a garden at the foot of the Space Needle.
sights.hours: Daily from ~10 AM (earlier in summer) to ~7 PM; hours vary by season

sights.name: Space Needle
sights.note: The 1962 World's Fair tower, with an outdoor deck and a rotating glass floor 500 ft up.
sights.hours: Daily ~9:30 AM–9 PM; hours vary by season

sights.name: Pike Place Market
sights.note: Seattle's century-old public market above the waterfront: fish throwers, produce stalls, crafts and the original Starbucks.
sights.hours: Market shops ~9 AM–6 PM daily; some restaurants open later

sights.name: The Museum of Flight
sights.note: A vast air and space museum at Boeing Field, with a Concorde, Air Force One and the original Boeing factory.

sights.name: Washington State Ferries (Seattle Ferry Terminal)
sights.note: Ferries from Colman Dock to Bainbridge Island and Bremerton give cheap skyline and Olympic Mountains views; walk-on fares are paid only westbound.

sights.name: Kerry Park
sights.note: A small Queen Anne hillside lookout with the classic postcard view of the Space Needle, downtown and Mount Rainier.

sights.name: Museum of Pop Culture
sights.note: Frank Gehry's crumpled-metal building houses exhibits on music, sci-fi, horror and games, including Nirvana and Jimi Hendrix.

sights.name: Sky View Observatory
sights.note: A 73rd-floor observation deck in the Columbia Center, higher than the Space Needle and with the Needle in the view.

sights.name: Alki Beach
sights.note: A long sandy West Seattle beach with a promenade and skyline views, best reached on the King County Water Taxi from Pier 50.
sights.hours: Beach park open ~4 AM–11:30 PM daily

sights.name: T-Mobile Park
sights.note: The Seattle Mariners' retractable-roof ballpark, a short walk from Stadium and King Street stations.
sights.hours: Game days, plus guided ballpark tours on select days

sights.name: Hiram M. Chittenden Locks
sights.note: The Ballard Locks lift boats between the lake and Puget Sound; a fish ladder shows salmon running in summer.
sights.hours: Grounds 7 AM–9 PM daily; visitor center shorter hours; free

sights.name: Klondike Gold Rush National Historical Park
sights.note: A free Pioneer Square museum on Seattle's role as outfitter for the 1897 Yukon gold rush.
sights.hours: ~10 AM–5 PM; fewer days in winter; free

sights.name: Seattle Central Library
sights.note: Rem Koolhaas's glass-and-steel library, free to explore, with a spiral book ramp and a 10th-floor reading room.
sights.hours: Mon–Thu 10 AM–8 PM, Fri–Sat 10 AM–6 PM, Sun noon–6 PM

sights.name: Seattle Aquarium
sights.note: Pier 59's aquarium of Puget Sound sea life, with sea otters, and a newer Ocean Pavilion of tropical reef fish across the street.

sights.name: Washington Park Arboretum
sights.note: 230 acres of trails and trees along Lake Washington, with the separately ticketed Seattle Japanese Garden at its south end.
sights.hours: Grounds open dawn to dusk daily; free

sights.name: Seattle Art Museum
sights.note: Downtown's main art museum, with Northwest Coast Native art and global collections behind the Hammering Man sculpture.

sights.name: University of Washington
sights.note: A Gothic-revival campus with Suzzallo Library's reading room and the Quad, famous for its cherry blossoms in late March.
sights.hours: Campus open daily; buildings keep their own hours

sights.name: Gas Works Park
sights.note: An old gas plant turned lakeside park, with rusting towers and a kite hill looking across Lake Union to downtown.

railStations.name: King Street Station
railStations.note: Amtrak hub: Cascades trains to Portland and Vancouver BC, the Coast Starlight and Empire Builder, plus Sounder commuter rail. International District/Chinatown Link station (1 and 2 Lines, on this map) is a 2-minute walk.
railStations.hours: Station ~6:00 AM–~11:00 PM; few trains after 9 PM

airports.name: Seattle-Tacoma International Airport
airports.transitNote: Link 1 Line stops at SeaTac/Airport station (on this map), a ~5-min walk through the parking garage skybridge from the terminal; ~40 min to Westlake downtown for the flat $3 fare. Taxis/rideshare ~$50–65, 25–40 min.
airports.hours: 1 Line: first train ~5:00 AM (~6:00 AM Sun), last ~1:00 AM (~midnight Sun)
